newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Profits drop on NZ livestock, cropping farms - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Profits drop on NZ livestock, cropping farms - SNZ.

text.p: The average net profit of cropping, mixed and other livestock farming declined 68 percent in 1994/95 against the previous year, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
Average net profit before tax was down to $7,100 against $22,300.
Gross incomes fell five percent and operating expenses rose four percent.
The main contribution was a fall in the book value of livestock reflecting lower sheep and beef prices.
Deer made a positive contribution with a 35 percent increase in receipts.
Expenses were up mainly due to feed, fodder and grazing costs, up 18 percent, electricity and fuel, up 13 percent, depreciation, up 13 percent, and interest paid, up 4 percent.
Kiwifruit and horticulture profits were up with kiwifturit farm net profits up to $22,900 from $9,500.
Total sales for kiwifruit farms tose to $143,200 from $106,400.
For all horticultural farms, profits increased to $25,700 from $19,400.
Operating expenditure increased nine percent to $163,000.
